category_title: Seniors who avoid writing tasks due to perceived difficulty and lack of process knowledge
minimal_context: The student is self-evaluating their writing draft using a correction goal sheet and a Likert scale in a 12th grade expository writing class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please self-evaluate your writing draft using the correction goal sheet and the four-point Likert scale, where 0 means 'need help with this' and 3 means 'personal best'.

STUDENT: I don't know how to grade my own work. I took an AP English class and that teacher never told me what I was doing wrong. She would just say I got an F.

TUTOR: Just look at what you wrote and try to pick a number on the scale.

STUDENT: I can't. Before this class I thought that I was the worst writer in the world. Without knowing where I did good and where I messed up, I just feel like I'm failing.

TUTOR: You need to finish the evaluation so you can get credit for the draft.

STUDENT: I'm not completing the assignment. I'm just embarrassed by my writing and I've lost hope of ever being successful.

options.A: Teach and practice self-calming strategies with the student, specifically focusing on managing strong feelings and calming anger.
options.B: Focus on process-oriented assessment rather than product-oriented assessment when the student evaluates their writing drafts.
options.C: Implement a group reinforcement contingency to provide the student with peer attention and a whole-class reinforcer for appropriate behavior.
options.D: Conduct sustained silent reading each Friday for an entire class period during the expository writing class.
